title: RFID Gift Cards — Contactless Stored-Value Cards
summary: RFID gift cards are ISO/IEC 7810 stored-value cards with a 13.56 MHz NFC chip that customers tap to redeem at the POS in under 1 second. The balance lives in the POS or gift-card system; each chip carries a unique UID that cannot be skimmed like a magnetic stripe. Chip options run from NTAG213 to AES-128 MIFARE DESFire EV3; custom-printed cards start at MOQ 500 with 12-15 business day lead times.
heroPoints: Tap-to-redeem: NFC gift cards process at the POS in under 1 second; no swiping, inserting or barcode scanning required.
Brand-building design: full-color printing, metallic foil, spot UV, die-cut shapes and custom packaging make your gift card a premium branded product that customers are proud to give.
Fraud-resistant: each NFC chip carries a unique, unclonable ID; unlike magnetic stripe gift cards, NFC gift cards cannot be skimmed or duplicated at the point of sale.
imageAlt: Custom-designed RFID gift card with NFC chip and premium printing

brief.label: Card body and form factor
items: ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 (85.60 × 53.98 × 0.76 mm) is the retail-POS standard; rack-friendly fit into every display unit, wallet and envelope already in the store.
Die-cut non-ID-1 shapes (circle, bottle silhouette, product cut-out) available for premium seasonal ranges; require bespoke tooling and do not fit ID-1 racks.

brief.label: Gift-card market context
items: Global gift-card market tracked by Mercator Advisory Group / PYMNTS / NRF; U.S. alone tops USD 170 B annually, with Europe close behind under the EU Gift Card Directive framework.
Breakage (unredeemed balance) runs 6–12 % across U.S. retail and is reported under ASC 606 / IFRS 15 revenue-recognition rules — the structural margin of the programme.

brief.label: Chip selection by programme tier
items: NTAG213 (144 B) — URL-based balance lookup for low-stakes retail and café programmes; the cheapest credible NFC gift card.
NTAG216 (888 B) — room for a promo payload plus the balance-URL; the default for mid-market retail.
MIFARE Classic 1K — sector-based balance storage for legacy POS stacks that read sectors directly (not recommended for new builds).
MIFARE DESFire EV3 — AES-128 encrypted stored-value for high-volume or high-value programmes; keeps the server the source of truth but authenticates every tap.

brief.label: Activation and anti-theft
items: Cards ship deactivated with zero balance; activation at POS (barcode-scan + PIN-reveal) prevents theft of pre-loaded inventory from the display rack.
Scratch-off PIN panel over a 4-digit or 6-digit activation PIN is the in-store standard; some programmes print the PIN as a VOID-on-lift overlay instead.

brief.label: Fraud posture — NFC vs mag-stripe
items: Magnetic-stripe gift cards are routinely skimmed off-rack with handheld readers; criminals clone the stripe and drain the balance after activation.
NFC cards carry a unique chip UID that a skimmer cannot replay against the POS; DESFire EV3 + AES-128 key diversification (AN10922) raises the bar to cryptographic attack.

brief.label: Digital overlay — tap-to-balance
items: NDEF URI record programmed to `https://brand.example.com/gc?uid={uid}` opens the balance page on a stock iPhone (iOS 12+ Background Tag Reading) or Android phone without app install.
Apple Wallet Passes and Google Wallet generic passes can mirror the physical card, but physical card still sells as a gift (the wallet overlay is not a substitute for the giftable object).

brief.label: Premium finishing — the gift ambience
items: Hot-foil stamping (gold / silver / copper / holographic), embossing and spot-UV varnish on ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 PVC is the standard gift-aesthetic stack.
Card carrier / hanger / envelope / magnetic-closure box are ordered with the card and sequenced on the packing line so the unit walks out as a giftable SKU.

brief.label: Regulatory stack — Europe
items: EU PSD2 (Directive (EU) 2015/2366) defines the 'limited-network' exemption under which most retailer-issued closed-loop gift cards operate without becoming e-money.
EU Consumer Rights Directive 2011/83/EU requires clear pre-contractual disclosure of expiry and fees on retailer gift cards.

brief.label: Regulatory stack — United States
items: U.S. CARD Act 2009 (Title IV of the Credit CARD Act, §402) prohibits expiry inside 5 years and restricts dormancy fees on retail gift cards; state-level escheatment rules layer on top.
U.S. state escheat rules (Delaware, California, New York) trigger unclaimed-property reporting on dormant balances — operational tax cost the programme owner carries.

brief.label: POS and back-end integration
items: Back-end gift-card processors (InComm, Blackhawk Network, Givex, CashStar, PayPoint) expose activation / redemption APIs that the POS calls on each tap.
In-store reader (HID Omnikey 5127CK, Feig CPR40, ACS ACR1252) sits on the POS lane and passes UID to the processor; latency target < 500 ms round-trip.

brief.label: Reloadable / multi-visit programmes
items: Reloadable NFC gift cards turn a one-time gift into a repeat-visit prepaid tool — the processor toggles a 'reloadable' flag on the card record; the chip itself does not change.
Reload channels: POS top-up, e-commerce reload page, and (for wallet-provisioned mirror passes) in-app top-up via Apple Pay / Google Pay.

brief.label: Production workflow and lead time
items: Artwork → pre-press proof → plate / RIP → offset (MOQ 500) or UV digital (MOQ 100) → lamination → punch → chip encoding (UID registration + NDEF URL) → scratch panel → optional packaging.
Lead time 12–15 business days; + 3–5 days for foil / emboss / die-cut; free samples after artwork lock.

sections.title: Why businesses upgrade to NFC gift cards from magnetic stripe
bullets: Gift card fraud: magnetic stripe gift cards are vulnerable to skimming and cloning; criminals use handheld readers to copy the stripe data in-store and drain the balance before the recipient attempts to use the card. NFC chip-based gift cards eliminate this attack vector; MIFARE DESFire EV3 adds AES-128 key diversification for high-value programs.

Checkout experience: swiping a magnetic stripe gift card often requires multiple attempts due to worn stripes; NFC tap processes in under 1 second and is reliable on the first attempt every time, reducing checkout friction and cashier frustration.

Premium gifting experience: customers purchasing gift cards as holiday and birthday presents want a product that feels like a gift, not a disposable plastic rectangle; premium NFC cards with foil stamping, embossing and custom packaging justify a higher perceived value.

Digital bridge (NFC gift cards can be programmed to open a web page when tapped on an iOS 12+ iPhone or NFC Android phone with no app install, linking recipients to your online store, gift card balance checker or promotional landing page) creating an omnichannel experience from a physical card.
Reloadable programs: NFC-enabled stored-value cards can be reloaded at the POS or online, turning a one-time gift into a repeat-visit tool that builds long-term customer relationships.

sections.title: NFC vs magnetic-stripe vs barcode gift cards

comparePanel.afterHeading: vs magnetic-stripe and barcode gift cards
before: Tap-to-redeem; reliable on first attempt; no mechanical wear on stripe or barcode.
Unique chip UID; DESFire EV3 adds AES-128 and per-card key diversification.
Opens a balance landing page on a stock phone — omnichannel loop with no app install.
Premium-finish friendly: foil, emboss, spot-UV; the card is kept as a gift object.
Higher unit cost (USD 0.30–2.50); the fraud and experience lift usually pays back.
after: Magnetic-stripe: cheapest per unit (USD 0.10–0.30) but routinely skimmed off the rack — documented industry-wide attack pattern.
Barcode / QR: cheap and paper-capable, but photo-capture-clonable and sensitive to print wear and wrinkling.
Mag-stripe / barcode carries no phone-tap affordance; omnichannel loop needs a separate printed URL or QR.
Both feel like disposable ephemera; the gifting ambience has to be rebuilt in packaging.
Regulatory stack (CARD Act / PSD2) is identical — the stored-value framework is independent of read interface.

sections.title: Breakage — the economics every programme owner reads first

dataHighlight.heading: Unredeemed-balance breakage as structural programme margin
dataHighlight.text: 6 to 12 % of gift-card dollars are never redeemed (NRF / Mercator / CEB analysts). This breakage is recognised as revenue under ASC 606 / IFRS 15 once the customer's right to redeem expires or the card balance is deemed improbable of being drawn down. For a USD 10 M annual programme, that is USD 600 k–1.2 M of structural margin — funds the premium-finish card, the processor fees and the fraud-control stack with room to spare. NFC cards do not mechanically change breakage, but the tap-to-balance-page loop tends to reduce breakage slightly (recipients discover and redeem balances they would otherwise forget), which is a feature most retailers want in the long run.
dataHighlight.source: NRF annual gift-card outlook + Mercator Advisory Group gift-card market report + ASC 606 / IFRS 15 revenue recognition guidance

sections.title: Anatomy of an NFC gift card — layers, coil, and the finish that does the selling
sections.intro: A gift card has one job the recipient notices — feeling like a gift — and one the POS notices: answering in under a second. Both are settled in the lamination stack. Under the foil and the spot-UV sit a copper antenna coil and a 13.56 MHz chip that never carries the balance, only the identity that unlocks it. Spec the finishes on the [custom card printing](/products/rfid-cards/nfc-card-custom-printing/) page and the secure chip tier on the [MIFARE DESFire EV3 card](/products/rfid-cards/mifare-desfire-ev3-card/) page.

image.alt: Two-panel diagram of an NFC gift card. Left, the lamination stack exploded: a printed front overlay carrying artwork and hot-foil; a PVC or PET core embedding the copper antenna coil and the NFC chip module; and a back overlay carrying the scratch-off PIN panel and signature strip. A bracket marks 0.76 mm assembled thickness on an 85.60 × 53.98 × 0.76 mm ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 body, with a note to keep foil, spot-UV and embossing off the scratch panel. Right, the tap-to-redeem path: the card coil couples inductively with a POS reader at 13.56 MHz, contactless and powered by the reader field; the chip carries only a unique UID that the POS or gift-card processor looks up to find the balance and post the deduction, in under 1 second with a < 500 ms round-trip.

bullets: Print stack: the front overlay carries the artwork, hot-foil, spot-UV and embossing; the back overlay carries the scratch-off PIN panel and signature strip.
Core: a PVC or PET core embeds the copper antenna coil and the NFC chip module — the coil harvests the reader's field, so there is no battery to fail.
Chip: NTAG213 (144 B) for a balance URL, NTAG216 (888 B) for a promo payload, MIFARE Classic 1K for legacy sector reads, or MIFARE DESFire EV3 with AES-128 for high-value programmes.
Geometry: 85.60 × 53.98 × 0.76 mm — the ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 body every retail rack, wallet and gift envelope is already built around.
Keep-out: foil, spot-UV and embossing stay clear of the scratch panel so the activation PIN reveals cleanly at the till.

sections.title: From print run to tap-to-redeem — the gift-card lifecycle
sections.intro: A gift card earns its keep in four moves: it is printed and encoded, it sits on the rack with no money on it, it is activated at the till, and then it is tapped — ideally more than once. The chip never changes across any of it; the processor just toggles a flag. Turn the one-time gift into a repeat visit with a [reloadable loyalty card](/products/rfid-cards/rfid-loyalty-card/) or a [membership card](/products/rfid-cards/rfid-membership-card/) built on the same silicon.

image.alt: A four-step left-to-right flow. One, print and encode: offset or UV digital print, UID plus an NDEF balance URL, scratch-PIN and packaging. Two, on the rack: ships deactivated with zero balance, worthless until sold. Three, activate at POS: scan the barcode, reveal the PIN, the processor loads the balance and the card flips live. Four, tap to redeem: tap in under 1 second, UID drives a balance lookup with a < 500 ms round-trip. A dashed reload loop returns to the POS for a repeat visit, and a bottom band notes that 6–12 % of loaded value is never redeemed and books as revenue under ASC 606 / IFRS 15.

checklist: Print & encode: artwork → offset or UV digital → lamination → punch → chip encoding (UID registration + NDEF balance URL) → scratch-PIN → packaging.
Ship deactivated: cards leave the factory with zero balance, so inventory taken off the display rack is worthless until it is activated.
Activate at POS: the cashier scans the barcode and reveals the PIN; the processor loads the initial balance and flips the card live in under a second.
Tap to redeem: the recipient taps at the lane; UID → processor balance lookup → deduction, with a < 500 ms round-trip target.
Reload or check balance: top up at the POS, on an e-commerce reload page, or in a wallet pass; a tap opens the balance page on any NFC phone.
Breakage settles: 6–12 % of loaded value is never redeemed and books as revenue under ASC 606 / IFRS 15 — the structural margin behind the whole programme.

faq.question: How is the balance stored and managed on NFC gift cards?
faq.answer: The balance is typically stored in your POS or gift card management system, not on the card itself. The NFC chip carries a unique ID that links to the account record in your system. When the customer taps the card, the POS reads the chip ID, looks up the balance, deducts the purchase amount and updates the record. This server-side approach is more secure than storing the balance on the card and enables online balance checking.

faq.question: Can recipients check their gift card balance on their phone?
faq.answer: Yes. If the card is programmed with an NDEF URL, the recipient taps the card on their NFC-enabled phone and a web page opens showing their current balance and transaction history. No app download required. This works on iPhone (XS and newer) and most Android phones with NFC.

faq.question: What is the MOQ and lead time for custom gift cards?
faq.answer: Custom-printed NFC gift cards: MOQ 500, lead time 12-15 business days from artwork approval. Premium features (foil stamping, embossing, die-cut shapes) add 3-5 business days. Gift card packaging (holders, envelopes, boxes): MOQ 500, produced concurrently with the cards. Contact us with your design concept for a quotation.

faq.question: Can we see samples before committing to a full gift-card run?
faq.answer: Yes. Proud Tek provides free samples once your artwork is locked, so you can check the print, foil, scratch-off PIN panel and chip encoding on a physical card before the main run. Send your design concept and target chip (NTAG213, NTAG216, MIFARE Classic 1K or MIFARE DESFire EV3) for a quotation; custom-printed cards are MOQ 500 with a 12-15 business day lead time from artwork approval.

faq.question: What printing, finishing and personalisation options are available on RFID gift cards?
faq.answer: Full-colour offset printing (MOQ 500) or UV digital (MOQ 100), with hot-foil stamping in gold, silver, copper or holographic, spot-UV varnish, soft-touch lamination, embossed logos and card numbers, and die-cut non-ID-1 shapes for seasonal ranges. Per-card variable data includes sequential card numbers, unique QR codes, 4-digit or 6-digit scratch-off PIN panels, and a pre-programmed NDEF balance URL. Premium finishes add 3-5 business days, and die-cut shapes require bespoke tooling.

faq.question: How are RFID gift cards encoded, activated and protected against theft?
faq.answer: Each card ships deactivated with a zero balance and a unique chip UID registered at encoding, and an NDEF URI record is written so a tap opens your balance page on iOS 12+ or NFC Android with no app install. At the point of sale the cashier scans the barcode, reveals the scratch-off PIN, and the processor loads the initial balance — so cards taken off the display rack before activation are worthless. For high-value programmes, MIFARE DESFire EV3 adds AES-128 and per-card key diversification (NXP AN10922) so a skimmer cannot replay the card against the POS.

faq.question: What gift-card regulations apply, and does RFID change compliance?
faq.answer: The regulatory stack is independent of the read interface — RFID does not change it. In the United States, the CARD Act of 2009 prohibits expiry inside 5 years and restricts dormancy fees, with state escheatment rules layering unclaimed-property reporting on top. In the EU, most retailer-issued closed-loop gift cards operate under the PSD2 (Directive (EU) 2015/2366) limited-network exemption, and the Consumer Rights Directive 2011/83/EU requires clear disclosure of expiry and fees. Because a closed-loop RFID gift card carries a UID rather than payment-card data, it typically stays outside PCI DSS scope; confirm the boundary with your processor at tender stage.
